title: Karn Nijjar
text:
Welcome
I’m Karn.
I’m a Master of Data Science student at UBC. I hail from Toronto, ON in Canada and I studied Actuarial and Financial Mathematics in my undergraduate degree at McMaster University.
I served as a reservist for three years in the Canadian Armed Forces before releasing with the rank of Bombardier. I also worked as a Management Trainee at Cintas for just over two years where I held roles in production, service, and sales.
After MDS, I hope to work as a Data Scientist at an organization that utilizes data in an ethical and meaningful way.

On the dataset
This dataset has information on penguins of three species from three islands in Antarctica.

title: Penguin body mass by species and sex (Python version)

Intent
We are going to examine how body mass differs between males and females in each species and how the species fare against each other in this regard.

section: Average body mass (g) by species and sex
text:
Average body mass (g) by species and sex
Now, let’s make a table that shows the average body mass in grams of the male and female penguins in each species.

avg_body_mass_table = (
  penguins_filtered
  .groupby(['species', 'sex'])['body_mass_g']
  .mean()
  .round()
  .reset_index(name = "average_body_mass_in_grams")
)

title: Penguin body mass by species and sex (Python version)
text:
Plotting our penguins
Now, let’s make a plot of our filtered penguin data.

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.boxplot(data = penguins_filtered, x = 'species', y = 'body_mass_g', hue = "sex", order = ['Adelie', 'Chinstrap', 'Gentoo'], hue_order = ['female', 'male'], ax = ax)
ax.set_xlabel("Species")
ax.set_ylabel("Body mass (grams)")
ax.legend(title = "Sex")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Body mass of penguins by sex and species

title: Penguin body mass by species and sex (Python version)
text:
Takeaways
Males have larger body masses than their female counterparts for all the species, most evidently in the Gentoo penguins.
Gentoo penguins have higher body masses than Adelie and Chinstrap penguins (whose body masses are not that different from one another).

text: Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. Released under CC0.

title: Penguin body mass by species and sex (R version)
text:
On the dataset
This dataset has information on penguins of different species that originate on islands in Antarctica.

title: Penguin body mass by species and sex (R version)
text:
Intent
We are going to investigate this dataset to find out how body mass differs between males and females in each species and how the species fare against one another in this regard.

title: Penguin body mass by species and sex (R version)
text:
Summoning the libraries

library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

section: Manipulating the dataset into a filtered version
text:
Manipulating the dataset into a filtered version
We are going to clean up the dataset by filtering out rows that do not have a value for body mass or sex. Then, let’s glimpse the new dataset penguins_filtered.

penguins_filtered <- penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g), !is.na(sex))

glimpse(penguins_filtered)

title: Penguin body mass by species and sex (R version)
section: Average body mass (g) by species and sex
text:
Average body mass (g) by species and sex
We are going to find average body mass (rounded to the closest non-decimal number) for males and females of every species in the dataset, formatting that information into a table.

avg_body_mass_table <- penguins_filtered |>
  group_by(species, sex) |>
  summarise(
    average_body_mass_in_grams = round(mean(body_mass_g)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(avg_body_mass_table)

title: Penguin body mass by species and sex (R version)
text:
Plotting our penguins
We are going to make a boxplot of the filtered penguins dataset. The plot will visualize the body mass (in grams) of both males and females in each species.

ggplot(penguins_filtered, aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Body mass (grams)", fill = "Sex") +
  theme_bw()







Figure 1: Body mass of penguins by species and sex

title: Penguin body mass by species and sex (R version)
text:
Takeaways
It seems that males are generally heavier than their female counterparts in each of the three species in the dataset. This is most prominent in Gentoo penguins.
Out of the three species, Gentoo penguins are the heaviest. Adelie and Chinstrap penguins do not seem to be too different in their average body masses.

title: About
text:
Why MDS
I chose a graduate education in data science because I had continued exposure to operational issues and redundancies that could have been addressed with the appropriate use of data. This data was already being collected, however, I observed that organizations were ill-equipped to derive any actionable outputs out of it (at least to the extent that was warranted). These observations, alongside my existing background in mathematics and statistics, pushed me to specialize in data science, where I hope to utilize the skills I will develop over the program to help organizations make the most of their data

Hobbies
My hobbies are rather simple but, I like to believe, far from boring. I enjoy film, music, cooking, and exercise. My favourite activities include weightlifting, swimming, and football (soccer). If I am not doing these things, I am probably just doing whatever my partner wants.
